full_details: You left the close in grey light, in new-soled shoes and the broad hat, with the oiled wallet on your back. You went by Ludgate and the Strand, and west by Knightsbridge and Kensington, and then by a lane onto the Uxbridge way. It cost a mile. At Uxbridge you ate Jacqueline's bread and cheese and paid one penny for a quart of ale. A watchman looked at the pack and let you through. A strap rubbed, and you stopped to set it. Near Chalfont the flint road ran through beeches, with wild thyme at the verge. You paid two pence for a loft over an alehouse, after bacon and pease-pottage, on last year's hay. You counted the same parcels, and then you took your shoes off. The left heel was raw.
one_sentence: You walked out at ten past four and slept in a loft at Chalfont for two pence.
title: A penny at the bridge
